changes: Main design changed from three A/B/C menus and B–C Eco choice to two 1:1 flat/function-grouped presentations with the same six options and proposed functions.

Grouped presentation separates adaptive conservation-policy Eco from fixed Light/Medium/High/ExtraHigh/Max. Shared item wording, option order, controls and responses held constant; group headings/spacing are intended presentation package, not pure naming effect.

Primary event is first-task Eco selection AND all three correct post-choice functional comprehension items, compared grouped-minus-flat with95% CI. Raw choice and comprehension remain separate outcomes; all randomized groups retained.
Three comprehension items, scoring0–3/all-correct criterion and do-not-know versus missing distinctions added to Appendix A.

Common authored X/Y evaluation independent of selected-mode execution retained. Initial versus post-comparison sufficiency ratings separated; perceived-sacrifice event uses post-comparison judgment and choosing X unchanged.

Recorded first action after common X/Y exposure precedes optional branches. X/Y unchanged use, editing, opening authored Z, selecting another mode, using neither and deferral distinguished. Later branches exploratory.
Compact Eco/High/Max menu retained as follow-up, not third main arm.
Pilot, sample/precision planning and analysis updated for joint primary endpoint. Main N, duration/compensation and final materials/logging still require specification before collection.
Korean-speaking adult LLM-user scope retained; English examples remain illustrative translations.
Standard Word fonts used for portability; all8 final pages visually verified, including final revised pages3/4 and unchanged-image confirmation for remaining pages.

scope_limits: Adaptive Eco is a proposed conceptual mapping requiring pilot validation, not implemented resource allocation.
Post-choice demonstration does not prove understanding preceded the initial choice, ecological motive, consent quality, or causal mediation.
Comprehension questions may prompt later reflection; later actions interpreted within shared study sequence.
Prototype branch choices do not establish actual task completion, long-term service use, resource savings or ecological benefit.
Quality preservation and environmental savings not success gates; no first-of-kind claim.
